curated.title: Daughters of the Dust: the Peazant family and their choices
curated.creator: Open Research Navigator / project team
curated.description: Begin with the film overview and its historical setting. The Peazant family is deciding who will leave the Sea Islands and how to carry family memory forward.
curated.why: A focused, age-aware starting point from the page you are already exploring.

curated.title: Julie Dash: who made the film?
curated.creator: Open Research Navigator / project team
curated.description: Explore Julie Dash as the writer and director of Daughters of the Dust, and why her filmmaking is an important part of Black American film history.
curated.why: The filmmaker's choices help explain what makes the film distinctive.

curated.title: Gullah Geechee cultural heritage and the Sea Islands
curated.creator: National Park Service
curated.description: The National Park Service introduces the Gullah Geechee Cultural Heritage Corridor and its cultural history across the southeastern coast. The external page covers difficult history in a general-public context.
curated.why: This provides historical and geographical context beyond the film's fictional family.

curated.title: Family, memory and leaving home
curated.creator: Open Research Navigator / project team
curated.description: As some family members prepare to leave the islands, the film asks how people remember their families and carry traditions into a different future.
curated.why: Connects a possible essay focus directly to the film's central family decisions.

curated.title: How the film tells its story
curated.creator: Open Research Navigator / project team
curated.description: The film moves between generations and memories rather than following just one person's journey. The connection pathway here is the project's interpretation, not a settled fact about cultural storytelling.
curated.why: Useful for thinking about how storytelling form makes the film's questions visible.

curated.title: Daughters of the Dust — film record
curated.creator: UCLA Film & Television Archive
curated.description: Archive record with production credits, synopsis, and the film's place in Black independent cinema. This is an outside archival page with an adult historical context.
curated.why: Gives a documented film record and a pathway into the L.A. Rebellion.

curated.title: L.A. Rebellion: Creating a New Black Cinema
curated.creator: UCLA Film & Television Archive
curated.description: UCLA explains its L.A. Rebellion collection and the work of Black filmmakers associated with the university.
curated.why: Connects Dash and her film to an artistic formation and institutional history.

curated.title: Daughters of the Dust — Library of Congress film record
curated.creator: Library of Congress
curated.description: A Library of Congress catalog record useful for identifying the film and checking information about it.
curated.why: Offers a library source independent of the project's own interpretation.

curated.title: Gullah Geechee: historical and geographical context
curated.creator: National Park Service
curated.description: An NPS historical introduction to the corridor, Gullah Geechee language, cultural practices and changing coastal communities.
curated.why: Provides a historical source that can be read alongside, but not conflated with, the film.
